ask: C++17. spsc.hpp and bench.cpp: lock-free single-producer/single-consumer bounded queue with std::atomic head/tail, acquire/release ordering, cache-line padding, capacity power of two with mask indexing, try_push/try_pop. bench.cpp pushes 10 million uint64 and verifies ordering, printing throughput. write the files.
prose:
There's a typo in `bench.cpp` — a stray single quote on the bandwidth output line (`'\n'` instead of `'\n'`). Let me fix that and write the corrected file.Both files are written. Here's what you have:

**spsc.hpp** — header-only `SPSCQueue<T>` template:
- Capacity rounds up to next power of two, indexing via `& mask_`
- `head_` and `tail_` are `std::atomic<size_t>`, each padded to its own 64-byte cache line (both before with `alignas` and after with trailing pad arrays) to eliminate false sharing
- `try_push` does relaxed read of `head_`, acquire load of `tail_` (to see the consumer's freed slot), placement-new, then release store of `head_` (publishing the element)
- `try_pop` does relaxed read of `tail_`, acquire load of `head_` (to see the producer's element), move-out, explicit destructor call, then release store of `tail_` (freeing the slot)
- Backing storage is aligned to `max(alignof(T), 64)` and allocated via sized aligned `operator new`; destructor drains any leftover elements before freeing
- No default construction of `T` needed — slots are raw `std::byte` storage until placement-new'd

**bench.cpp** — two-thread benchmark:
- Default pushes 10M `uint64_t` values (override via `argv[1]`)
- Producer spins on `try_push` with `yield`; consumer spins on `try_pop` with `yield`, verifying each popped value equals the expected counter (strict FIFO check)
- Reports element count, elapsed time, ops/s, bandwidth in B/s, and PASS/FAIL on ordering
- `producer_done` atomic prevents a false-empty race at the end

Build and run:

```
g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -pthread -o bench bench.cpp
./bench
```

Expected throughput on a modern CPU is in the low hundreds of millions of ops/s range, since the hot path is one relaxed load, one acquire load, one store, and one release store per operation with no allocation or system calls.
